# op — OpenProject CLI

Lightweight Perl CLI for the [OpenProject](https://www.openproject.org/) REST API (v3). Zero non-core Perl dependencies.

## Example Usage

```bash
tools/op help                      # show help
tools/op project list              # list all projects
tools/op project create "Neo-Mach" neo-mach
tools/op project get <id|slug>
tools/op project update 3 name="New Name"
tools/op project delete <id|slug>

tools/op wp list                   # list tickets in default project
tools/op wp list --status New --priority High
tools/op wp list --project gnu-mach-hurd
tools/op wp create "Port USB stack" --type Milestone --priority High
tools/op wp update 42 status="In progress" subject="Updated"
tools/op wp delete 42
tools/op wp types|statuses|priorities   # reference data

tools/op board list                 # list boards in the project
tools/op board summary              # Kanban overview: columns, counts,
                                    #   open/closed, types, hot items
tools/op board summary 11           # specific board by id or name
tools/op board summary --project neo-mach

tools/op config                    # show active .env settings
```

## Configuration

Read from `.env` in the project root:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `OPENPROJECT_URL` | Server base URL (e.g. `http://localhost:8080`) |
| `OPENPROJECT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token |
| `OPENPROJECT_USERNAME` | Display user |
| `OPENPROJECT_PROJECT_ID` | Default target project for `wp` commands |

Override the default project with `--project <id|slug>` on any `wp` subcommand.

## Dependencies

Only core Perl modules (v5.28+): `LWP::UserAgent`, `HTTP::Request`, `JSON::PP`, `Getopt::Long`. No CPAN installs needed.

# Kainos-Logos — Project Plan

> *καινός* (kainos) = new · *λόγος* (logos) = word / reason / ordering principle
>
> **The New Logos**: a cognitive architecture where a neural "language organ" maps
> natural language ↔ a formal Semantic IR, and all durable knowledge lives in a
> mutable, inspectable **CODEX** — an explicit semantic graph with provenance,
> context, time, epistemic state, and an **EXCEPTION** boundary.

## What this folder is

A hierarchical, executable plan. It starts at the level of vision and principles
and drills down — architecture → phases → actions → individual tasks — until the
leaves are concrete, ordered, verifiable steps.

## How to navigate

| Path | What it is |
|------|------------|
| [`00-north-star.md`](00-north-star.md) | The vision in one page + measurable success criteria. Start here. |
| [`01-principles.md`](01-principles.md) | Non-negotiable design invariants. Every decision must not violate these. |
| [`02-glossary.md`](02-glossary.md) | The controlled vocabulary (TERM, CODEX, EXCEPTION, …). |
| [`03-adr.md`](03-adr.md) | Architecture Decision Records. Living log of choices + rationale. |
| [`10-architecture/`](10-architecture/README.md) | The full system design, layer by layer. |
| [`20-roadmap.md`](20-roadmap.md) | Phase sequence, dependency graph, and the *compounding* contract. |
| [`30-phases/`](30-phases/README.md) | Phase-by-phase plans, each drilling to concrete actions. |
| [`40-testing/`](40-testing/README.md) | Test strategy, metrics, benchmarks, harness design. |
| [`90-appendices/`](90-appendices/prior-art.md) | Prior art, risks, open research questions, proposed repo layout. |

## The executable runbook

[`../action-steps/`](../action-steps/README.md) is the **operational** sibling of this
folder: 20 self-contained, sequential, prompt-like directives (plus a one-page
`00-CONTEXT.md` bootstrap). Each directive maps to the `P*.xx` actions below and can
be executed by a fresh agent without re-reading this plan. Read the plan for *why*;
follow `action-steps/` for *what to type*.

## The four phases (in order)

1. **Phase 0 — Foundation** (`30-phases/phase-0-foundation/`): scaffolding, CODEX
   data model, Semantic IR, test harness. No intelligence yet — just the substrate.
2. **Phase 1 — Regex** (`30-phases/phase-1-regex/`): the first proof of concept.
   Natural-language regex descriptions → Semantic IR → PCRE → executable tests.
3. **Phase 2 — 20 Questions** (`30-phases/phase-2-20questions/`): the active-learning
   training environment that exercises EXCEPTION, information gain, and persistent
   memory.
4. **Phase 3 — Generalization** (`30-phases/phase-3-generalization/`): the
   full-realized, task-agnostic architecture (multi-modal hooks, distributed
   CODEX, φ/Fibonacci numerics).

> The document's requested order is regex-first, then 20 Questions, then the
> full architecture. This plan preserves that ordering while inserting a
> Phase 0 because *both* later phases need the same substrate, and building it
> once is exactly the "compounding effect" the project depends on.

## The compounding contract

Every phase must **leave behind reusable artifacts** for the next phase and must
**test a specific architectural claim**, not just "build a thing". See
[`20-roadmap.md`](20-roadmap.md) for the explicit claim → artifact → test mapping.

# 00 — North Star

## The vision (one paragraph)

Build **Kainos-Logos**: a machine where a *neural language kernel* translates messy
human input into a formal **Semantic IR**, all durable knowledge is stored in an
explicit, inspectable **CODEX** (a graph of TERMS, typed RELATIONSHIPS, CONTEXT,
SOURCE, provenance, time, and epistemic state with an **EXCEPTION** boundary), and a
**Reasoner** searches, constrains, and verifies before a *realizer* turns the result
back into language. The neural component learns **how to operate on knowledge**; the
CODEX **accumulates the knowledge itself** — so the system keeps learning without
retraining its neural parameters.

## The core claim to prove (falsifiable)

> A small neural language interface coupled to a persistent, explicitly structured
> semantic memory can achieve competitive reasoning while learning new knowledge
> **without modifying its neural parameters**.

## Success criteria (measurable, in priority order)

1. **Persistent memory** — the system learns a term/fact in one session, is
   restarted (neural weights unchanged), and still uses that knowledge correctly.
2. **Compositional generalization** — it solves combinations of abstractions that
   never co-occurred in training (train on "three digits" + "optional" separately,
   test "three digits, optionally followed by a hyphen and two letters").
3. **Honest uncertainty** — it distinguishes *inferable* from *searchable* from
   *must-ask-the-human*, and abstains or clarifies instead of hallucinating.
4. **Inspectable reasoning** — every conclusion exposes the TERMS, constraints,
   traversals, and EXCEPTION depth that produced it. No opaque "probably".
5. **Compounding artifacts** — every phase leaves behind reusable substrate the next
   phase actually uses (measured by "lines reused vs. rewritten").

## What we are NOT trying to prove (scope guards)

- Not "replace transformers everywhere."
- Not "φ is magically optimal" — the φ/Fibonacci numerics are an isolated,
  *optional*, benchmarked experiment (Phase 3), never a dependency of Phases 0–2.
- Not "build AGI." The first claim is narrow: *can we separate learning from
  remembering, pattern recognition from reasoning, and knowledge from language?*

## The one-line test of everything

> **Can the system discover an abstraction that its designer did not explicitly
> put into the ontology?**
>
> If yes, we crossed the boundary from "fills slots in a predefined framework" to
> "expands the space in which it reasons." That is the whole point.

# 01 — Principles (non-negotiable design invariants)

Every design decision, code review, and phase-exit check is evaluated against these.
If a decision violates one, it is wrong until amended by an ADR in [`03-adr.md`](03-adr.md).

## P1 — Assertions, not facts

The CODEX never stores "the truth". It stores **assertions**: subject + relation +
object **wrapped in** provenance, source, context, validity interval, and epistemic
state. `CAPITAL_OF(France, Paris)` is stored as an assertion with `source`,
`confidence`, `context`, and `status`, never as a bare edge.

## P2 — The neural model is the language organ, not the brain

The neural component (a.k.a. "language kernel") does exactly two things:
`text ↔ Semantic IR` and hypothesis *proposal*. It must not be the store of durable
knowledge. Its weights can be frozen while the system keeps learning.

## P3 — The CODEX is the single source of truth for durable knowledge

Any durable fact lives in the CODEX, nowhere else. Transient context lives in
working memory. If two subsystems disagree about a fact, the CODEX holds the
disagreement (see P6), not a blended weight.

## P4 — Everything is a TERM

Terms are independently addressable semantic nodes, rotatable and searchable
orthogonally through their relationship neighborhoods. `CAPITAL_OF`, `country`,
`city`, `France`, `Paris` are each first-class TERMs; the record is the *pattern of
relationships between them*, not a rigid row.

## P5 — EXCEPTION ≠ impossible

The CODEX has a first-class representation for *unexplored / insufficiently
characterized* valid combinations (EXCEPTION), which is categorically different from
*impossible* (hard constraint violation). `TREE ∈ ANIMAL` is impossible;
`electronic + edible` is an EXCEPTION until characterized. Never conflate them.

## P6 — Contradiction is a signal, not an error

Two disagreeing assertions are *preserved*, not averaged. A recurring contradiction
is evidence of a **missing dimension** and should drive ontology expansion
(higher-order TERM), not probability blending.

## P7 — Semantic IR decouples the pipeline

Perception, reasoning, and realization are separated by a formal Semantic IR so that
any layer can be swapped or scaled independently (and later, modalities can share the
same IR).

## P8 — Measure, don't argue

Every architectural claim becomes a benchmarked experiment with a falsifiable
hypothesis, a metric, and a success threshold *before* it is believed. No unfalsifiable
"Fibonacci = intelligence" claims.

## P9 — Inspectability is a first-class feature

Never hide the CODEX. Every answer exposes its evidence chain and EXCEPTION depth.
This is both a debugging tool and the product's differentiator.

## P10 — Start small, scale later

No premature generalization. Phase 0/1 use the smallest substrate that can falsify
the core claim. Optimize (GPU, distributed, φ-numerics) only after the mechanism is
proven on a tiny domain.

## P11 — Capabilities are declared, not implied

The system may only plan over explicitly declared capabilities (TERMs with
preconditions/effects in the CODEX). A goal with no valid plan is a **first-class
outcome** — named capability gap + nearest viable plan. Never a hallucinated
action (supplemental-ideas integration; ADR-0011).

## P12 — Memory is recursively addressable structure; promotion is explicit

Working memory is not a bigger context window: it is a recursively nestable
WORKSPACE of queryable IRs with lifetimes, and nothing moves from working memory
into the CODEX except a deliberate, provenance-carrying promotion (ADR-0012).

# 02 — Glossary (controlled vocabulary)

These terms are used with fixed meanings throughout the plan and (later) the code.
Do not invent synonyms; extend here instead.

## Core entities

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **TERM** | An independently addressable semantic node (concept, entity, relation, operator, constraint, source…). Has an ID, one or more labels, and a semantic neighborhood. Everything is a TERM. |
| **RELATIONSHIP** | A typed, directed edge between TERMs: `SUBJECT --RELATION--> OBJECT`. Types include `is_a`, `part_of`, `causes`, `enables`, `requires`, `prevents`, `implies`, `correlates_with`, `precedes`, `followed_by`, `located_at`, `has_property`, etc. |
| **ASSERTION** | A relationship **wrapped in metadata**: provenance, source, context, validity interval, epistemic state, confidence. The atomic unit of CODEX storage. |
| **CONTEXT** | The conditions under which a relationship holds (domain, time, perspective, role, modality…). Relationships are indexed *by context*, not globally. |
| **SOURCE** | First-class TERM describing where an assertion came from: URI, media type, version, hash, retrieved-at, authority, accessibility. |

## The substrate

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **CODEX** | The persistent semantic substrate: a graph store of TERMs + typed RELATIONSHIPs + CONTEXT + SOURCE + provenance + EXCEPTION. The single source of truth for durable knowledge. |
| **Working Memory** | Transient, per-session state (active entities, hypotheses, goals, recent referents). Not durable. |
| **Semantic IR** | The formal intermediate representation that all layers speak. A serializable, language-independent structure (entities, relations, events, constraints, quantifiers, modality, time). |

## The pipeline

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Language Kernel** | The neural (or initially rule-based) component mapping `text ↔ Semantic IR` and proposing candidate interpretations. The "language organ". |
| **Reasoner / Solver** | Searches the CODEX, applies constraints, checks consistency, expands/contracts search depth. Produces a *verified* state or an *unresolved* state. |
| **Realizer** | Maps a verified Semantic IR back to natural language (surface realization). |
| **Execution Fabric** | The heterogeneous runtime (CPU graph traversal, GPU bitwise/parallel ops, DB persistence) that executes compiled Semantic IR operations. |

## Assertion `status` (lifecycle states)

An assertion's `status` field — how established a particular assertion is:

`candidate` · `established` · `disputed` · `obsolete` · `hypothesis` ·
`ambiguous` · `contradicted` · `inapplicable`

These are **not** the same list as the uncertainty states below; do not mix them.

## Uncertainty states (query/solver output)

When the solver answers a query it reports *which situation* the uncertainty is in
— a probability alone cannot distinguish these:

| State | Meaning | Typical cause |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| **KNOWN** | Verified/established under stated context. | — |
| **UNKNOWN** | No assertion on record. | never encountered |
| **AMBIGUOUS** | Multiple interpretations remain viable. | underspecified input |
| **HYPOTHETICAL** | Proposed but unverified. | inference, not observation |
| **CONTRADICTED** | Evidence supports incompatible interpretations. | conflicting sources |
| **INAPPLICABLE** | The relationship doesn't apply in this context. | wrong context selected |
| **IMPOSSIBLE** | Hard constraint violation (not merely unknown). | ontology constraint broken |

(`IMPOSSIBLE` overlaps the exception taxonomy below because a violated hard
constraint is also an EXCEPTION state — P5 keeps the categories distinct from
merely-*unknown*.)

## The knowledge boundary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **EXCEPTION** | A *representable but insufficiently characterized* valid combination of TERMs/relationships. Its states: `UNSEEN`, `UNRESOLVED`, `AMBIGUOUS`, `CONFLICTING`, `UNVERIFIED`, `REQUIRES_CONTEXT`, `IMPOSSIBLE`. |
| **EXCEPTION depth / cost (E)** | `depth × ambiguity × lack_of_evidence`. Determines the runtime escalation: infer → search deeper → retrieve evidence → ask the human. |
| **Coverage(T, C)** | `verified_combinations / encountered_combinations` for a TERM `T` in context `C`. Measures "how well does the system understand this term?". |

## Memory tiers

`ephemeral` (next utterance) · `session` (this conversation) · `episodic` (event
memory) · `semantic` (generalized knowledge) · `procedural` (reusable how-to) ·
`hypothesis` (unverified candidate) — separated explicitly, never mashed into one
parameter space. The *containers* for the transient tiers are **WORKSPACE** objects
(see "The substrate" below and `10-architecture/workspace-memory.md`); the
`project` lifetime sits between `session` and `long_term`.

## The projection layer (Phase 3, ADR-0011)

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **WORKSPACE** | A bounded, named, lifetime-scoped, recursively nestable container of IRs, hypotheses, constraints, plans, exceptions, and references. Memory as queryable structure, not a bigger context window (P12). |
| **Lifetime** | A workspace's scope: `EPHEMERAL \| SESSION \| PROJECT \| LONG_TERM`. Content migrates only by explicit promotion. |
| **Promotion** | The deliberate operation that writes a workspace IR's relationships into the CODEX as *candidate* assertions with provenance (`source=workspace_<id>`). Never implicit. |
| **CAPABILITY** | A first-class TERM declaring an operation the system may invoke, with `PRECONDITION`, `INPUT`, `EFFECT`, `COST`. The planner may use only declared capabilities (P11). |
| **PLAN** | A sequence of declared capabilities whose effect application takes a start state to a terminal state satisfying the goal — a proof, not a guess. |
| **NO VALID PLAN** | The first-class result for an unachievable goal: names the missing capability and gives the nearest viable plan. Never a hallucinated action. |
| **PROJECTION** | The step `Response = Realize(Project(Parse(Input), Context, Knowledge, Capabilities, Goal))` — goal-directed semantic transformation. |
| **RESPONSE CONTRACT** | The per-interaction-type shape of a correct response (REQUEST/QUESTION/COMMAND/ASSERTION/CORRECTION/impossible/ambiguous), checked at realization. |
| **Semantic temperature** | The creativity parameter over *constrained* graph traversal: varies which valid path is taken, never whether an established fact holds (novelty must not violate P5/P6). |

## Learning loop

`observe → interpret → hypothesize → verify → consolidate → generalize` — the
learning objective replaces "predict next token" with "shrink the EXCEPTION space
and expand the ontology".

# 03 — Architecture Decision Records (ADR)

Living log. Each entry: status, decision, rationale, consequences, supersedes.
A decision here is binding until a later ADR overturns it.

## ADR-0001 — Languages: Python (in Docker) for prototypes, Perl for regex glue, Rust long-term

- **Status:** Accepted — supersedes the earlier "Python only" decision.
- **Decision:**
  - **Prototype Phases 0–2 in Python ≥3.11**, running inside a pinned Docker image
    (ADR-0010) so the host stays clean.
  - **Perl** for regex-specific scripting and — especially — the **regex judge**
    (compile + full-match verdicts). Perl is the canonical home of regex and is
    more ubiquitous than Python for it.
  - **Rust** as the long-term implementation language for the final architecture:
    port the proven core and copy-in/translate any crates the ecosystem lacks.
- **Rationale:** Python is fastest to *falsify* the claims, but its venv is fragile —
  Docker makes the toolchain reproducible data instead. Perl gives a real regex
  engine for the judge at zero new deps. Rust fits the end-state (persistent graph
  store, constraint solving, bit-level φ ops) and honors ADR-0006's "rewrite only
  what's proven."
- **Consequences:** The regex judge lives in Perl. The core (CODEX/IR/reasoner) stays
  language-agnostic at the IR boundary (ADR-0003), so a Rust port is a drop-in
  replacement behind the same interfaces. No premature Rust.

## ADR-0002 — CODEX storage: abstraction over SQLite first, graph DB later

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Define a `CodexStore` interface (add/remove/query assertions). Ship a
  SQLite-backed implementation (quad table + indices) for Phases 0–1. Optionally add
  a `networkx` in-memory implementation for fast experiments.
- **Rationale:** The document notes a graph DB is a fine *storage engine* but the
  *model* is "assertions, not facts". SQLite is zero-ops, inspectable, portable, and
  keeps us from over-investing in a graph engine before the semantics are stable.
- **Consequences:** A `CodexStore` port (Neo4j/JanusGraph/…) is a Phase 3 concern.
  Inspectability (P9) is served by a `sqlite3` CLI + dump tool.

## ADR-0003 — Semantic IR serialization: JSON

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Semantic IR is a JSON-serializable structure with a versioned schema
  (`ir.schema.json`), not a Python object graph on the wire.
- **Rationale:** Language/modality agnostic (P7), trivially inspectable (P9),
  diffable for provenance/debugging, and testable with golden files.
- **Consequences:** A `Codec` validates IR against the schema at every boundary.

## ADR-0004 — Language Kernel: deterministic grammar first, LLM second

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Phase 1's language kernel is a **deterministic, hand-written parser
  over a restricted English grammar** (regex-description subset). The LLM path is a
  drop-in `LanguageKernel` implementation added later, so the A/B experiment
  (conventional vs. CODEX) is clean.
- **Rationale:** The core claim (P2) is about *separating knowledge from language*,
  not about parsing skill. A deterministic parser removes a confound, is free, and
  can be run in CI. The LLM becomes a second implementation of the same interface.
- **Consequences:** The `LanguageKernel` interface is the contract; the grammar
  subset is defined in `30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md`.

## ADR-0005 — Every phase ships a falsifiable experiment

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** No phase is "done" until its named experiment runs green in CI and
  its metric is reported. "Building" is not a deliverable; "demonstrating a claim"
  is.
- **Rationale:** P8 (measure, don't argue) and the north-star success criteria.
- **Consequences:** `40-testing/harness.md` defines the experiment runner contract.

## ADR-0006 — φ/Fibonacci numerics are isolated and optional

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** The φ-positional number system ("power stepping") is a Phase 3,
  standalone, benchmark-gated experiment. It is **never** a dependency of the CODEX
  schema or the Phase 0–2 pipeline.
- **Rationale:** The document itself rates it ★★★★★ but explicitly warns against
  assuming superiority. It must be tested on its own metric
  ("useful neural computation per bit-op") without entangling core semantics.
- **Consequences:** Core CODEX stores strengths as ordinary numbers (or compact
  ints) with a `Numerics` strategy seam reserved for Phase 3.

## ADR-0007 — Repo layout: `src/kainos` package + `tests/` mirror

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Monorepo, single package `kainos`, mirroring `tests/`. Plan lives in
  `plan/`, specs in `specs/`, data in `data/`. See `90-appendices/repo-layout.md`.
- **Rationale:** One package keeps the compounding import graph simple and lets the
  CODEX core be reused by regex, 20Q, and generalization phases.
- **Consequences:** Public package name `kainos` is reserved; phases add submodules,
  never sibling packages.

## ADR-0008 — Provenance and epistemic state are mandatory, not optional

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Every assertion in the CODEX carries `source`, `context`, `validity
  interval`, `confidence`, and `status` from the very first line of Phase 0. There
  is no "bare edge" escape hatch.
- **Rationale:** P1/P6 and the document's repeated warning that these aren't
  secondary features but "part of the learning architecture itself".
- **Consequences:** The CODEX schema in `10-architecture/codex.md` has these fields
  non-nullable; tests assert their presence.

## ADR-0009 — Regex judge runs under Perl's regex engine

- **Status:** Accepted — supersedes the earlier "Python `re`" decision.
- **Decision:** The regex **judge** (compile + full-match verdicts on generated
  examples) runs under **Perl's regex engine**, not Python's `re`. The emitter
  targets the Perl/PCRE-compatible construct set we emit (no backrefs/recursion
  initially).
- **Rationale:** Perl is the canonical, ubiquitous regex host; its engine is a
  superset of PCRE. Python's `re` is not PCRE and has Unicode-aware shorthand
  divergence. User direction: "PCRE is Perl, we have Perl."
- **Consequences:** The judge is a small Perl script invoked by the harness; the
  emitted subset is validated against it. The core (CODEX/IR/reasoner) stays Python
  (in Docker). If an in-process judge is ever needed, the Python `regex` module is a
  fallback, but Perl is canonical.

## ADR-0010 — Idempotent Docker build; every dependency is pinned data

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** All build/run tooling (Python, Perl, llama.cpp, libraries) is declared
  in an in-repo `Dockerfile` + pinned lockfile. Development and tests run **inside**
  the container; the host is never modified. Pin every version: base image digest,
  Python, pip hashes, llama.cpp commit.
- **Rationale:** "Every system dependency is now data" — reproducibility and a clean
  host, avoiding the venv horror. Matches the compounding/reproducibility goals
  (seeded, hash-pinned results).
- **Consequences:** `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, and a lockfile become part of the
  repo. CI builds the image and runs the suite inside it. Phases 0–2 are CPU-only in
  the container; GPU (Vulkan) pass-through is a Phase-3 concern.

## ADR-0011 — Projection: capabilities are first-class TERMS; planning runs over the CODEX

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Add a projection layer (Phase 3, directive 21): capabilities are
  explicit TERMS with `PRECONDITION`/`INPUT`/`EFFECT`/`COST` assertions in the
  CODEX; the reasoner gains a bounded plan search (precondition-checked effect
  application until a terminal state satisfies the goal). A goal with no valid plan
  is a first-class **NO VALID PLAN** result (named capability gap + nearest viable
  plan + search trace). Traversal may be stochastic under a **semantic temperature**
  parameter, but novelty may never violate established facts or hard constraints.
- **Rationale:** Principle P11 and the supplementary design ("goal-directed
  semantic transformation"): the hard problem is not parsing or language generation
  — it is deciding, from a structured goal, which declared transformations satisfy
  it. LLMs "just answer" and fabricate capabilities; a declared-capability planner
  turns "I can't, but here's the nearest viable plan" into a *verifiable* output.
  It reuses the machinery already built: information-gain question selection (A1)
  picks clarification questions over *plan branches*; EXCEPTION states cover the
  failure taxonomies.
- **Consequences:** `src/kainos/projection/` is Phase 3 only and must not alter
  Phase 0–2 pipelines. E3.6 (X1/X2) is benchmark-gated with **simulated**
  capabilities — no real side effects. Response contracts are data (per interaction
  type), extendable without new code paths.

## ADR-0012 — WORKSPACE memory: recursive IR containers with explicit promotion

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision:** Add a `kainos.workspace` module (Phase 3, directive 22): a WORKSPACE
  is a bounded, named, lifetime-scoped (`EPHEMERAL|SESSION|PROJECT|LONG_TERM`),
  recursively nestable container of Semantic IRs + hypotheses + constraints + plans
  + exceptions + references. Long-term content enters the CODEX **only** via an
  explicit `promote()` that writes candidate assertions with
  `provenance.source = workspace_<id>`, which then pass ordinary verification.
  Sources (documents) are held as SOURCE objects with **versioned analysis IRs** —
  the document never becomes the knowledge.
- **Rationale:** Principle P12 and the supplementary design: persistent-memory
  problems and unbounded-context bloat are solved by making memory a recursively
  addressable space of structured thought. Implicit promotion is the corruption
  path ("penguins can fly" from one joking session); explicit, provenance-carrying
  promotion keeps the CODEX's epistemic discipline (P1, ADR-0008) intact. Phases
  1–2 already use de-facto workspaces (20Q game state, pipeline results) — this
  generalizes them without changing the proven pipeline.
- **Consequences:** `src/kainos/workspace/` is Phase 3 only; E3.7 (X3) verifies
  queryability, recursion, and promotion discipline. Distributed nodes (step 19)
  may exchange workspace IRs as future deltas, but the Phase 3 protocol stays
  assertion-delta-only unless E3.7 shows a need.

## Log discipline

Append-only: new decisions get the next number; a superseded ADR stays, marked
superseded, with a pointer to its replacement (as ADR-0001/0009 demonstrate).

# 04 — Reality Check (pre-development)

Honest audit of what's actually true before we write code. Corrected 2026-08-19 for
hardware, toolchain, and scope decisions from the project owner.

## 1. Environment reality (verified 2026-08-19)

| Fact | Status | Consequence |
|------|--------|-------------|
| Host | **AMD Strix Halo** — Gmktec EVO-X2, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 128 GB DDR5 @ 8000 MT/s (unified memory) | no CUDA anywhere; GPU compute = Vulkan or experimental ROCm |
| GPU | Radeon RDNA 3.5 iGPU (40 CU) sharing the 128 GB | ideal for large local GGUFs; offload via **Vulkan** (ROCm on Strix Halo is still experimental) |
| **Thermal** | historically EC-gated hard power-off under heavy load; owner now runs **low-power mode — not a current constraint** | no special benchmark throttling for now |
| Python | 3.12.3 ✓ (host), venv available but PEP 668 managed | **run in Docker** (ADR-0010), don't pollute the host |
| Perl | present (system) | the regex judge lives in Perl (ADR-0009) |
| dev deps | pytest/mypy/ruff/hypothesis **missing** on host | installed inside the pinned Docker image, not the host |
| git | repo initialized, identity configured | keep committing as we go |
| local LLM | `llama-server` + GGUF models (Qwen3.6-27B, GLM-4.7-Flash, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, …) | E1.5 baseline runs fully offline |
| prior-art stance | owner: "prior art is to borrow from; our approach is new; overfit, so be it" | see §2 |

## 2. Scope: where our effort actually goes

Owner's ruling settles it: **we don't gate on prior art.** Prior art is a *library* —
we borrow datasets (e.g. `NL-RX-Synth`, `regel`) and the conventional-model baseline
where it saves time, and we don't spend cycles defending novelty.

What that ruling means for focus: the claims worth proving are the ones a compiler or
a frozen LLM **cannot** do — because those are the only ones that distinguish us and
the only ones worth our time:

1. **C2 — persistent learning without retraining** (teach → restart → still know).
2. **C3 — honest uncertainty** ("I don't know, but here's how to find out").
3. **A5 — contradiction expands the ontology** (new dimension, not averaged weights).
4. **A1 — active information-gain question selection** (20Q).

The E1.5 A/B still runs (we need a fair *conventional* comparator to claim "B > A"),
but that's borrowing a baseline, not seeking validation.

## 3. Regex engine (decided — ADR-0009)

Perl's regex engine is the judge. It's the canonical, ubiquitous regex host and a
superset of PCRE. Python's `re` (non-PCRE, Unicode `\d`) is **not** used for judging.
The emitter targets the Perl/PCRE-compatible construct set we emit; the judge is a
small Perl script the harness calls.

## 4. Kill criteria (null hypotheses we commit to before building)

- **K1:** If the teach→restart→reuse loop (C2) does not survive a restart with frozen
  kernel, the "knowledge separated from weights" claim is dead. **Stop or redesign.**
- **K2:** If, on the *novel* claims (C2/C3/A5), the CODEX adds no measurable benefit
  over a plain `dict` + compiler of equivalent complexity, the architecture is
  overhead. **Stop.**
- **K3:** If contradiction→dimension (A5) produces garbage terms that a human can't
  sign off on after one canonical conflict, the "self-expanding ontology" claim is
  unfalsifiable. **Constrain it or drop it.**
- **K4 (gated):** φ/Fibonacci numerics/topology must win a benchmark with a margin or
  be recorded **reject**. Already encoded in ADR-0006.

## 5. Decisions locked (with the owner's direction applied)

| Decision | Locked |
|----------|--------|
| Toolchain | Idempotent Docker image; every dependency pinned as data (ADR-0010) |
| Regex judge | Perl (ADR-0009) |
| Prototype language | Python, **inside Docker** only (ADR-0001) |
| Long-term language | Rust — port proven core, translate/copy crates (ADR-0001) |
| E1.5 LLM runtime | local `llama-server` + one pinned small GGUF; offline |
| E1.5 timing | deferred until C2/C3/A5 are green |
| GPU | defer; CPU-only in-container for Phases 0–2 |

## 6. The cheap pre-dev spike (do this before Phase 0 scaffolding)

A ~2-hour throwaway, run inside the Docker image, to validate the two riskiest
assumptions:

1. 5 sentences hand-pumped through `parse → IR → emit → (Perl judge)`.
2. A 20-line CODEX: teach one term → serialize → reload → resolve (proves C2's
   mechanism end-to-end before building the full store).

Keep it CPU-only and short — for fast iteration, not a thermal constraint. If the spike succeeds, Phase 0 is
de-risked; if persistence surprises us, fix the schema before committing to
`SqliteCodexStore`.

## 7. Immediate next actions (ordered)

1. Author `Dockerfile` + pinned lockfile (Python, Perl, dev deps, llama.cpp if needed).
2. Build the image; confirm `pytest`/`perl` run inside it.
3. Run the §6 spike inside the container.
4. Commit; then start `action-steps/01-scaffold.md`.

# 20 — Roadmap

## Phase sequence

```
Phase 0  FOUNDATION      substrate (CODEX + IR + harness)
   │
   ▼
Phase 1  REGEX           first PoC: NL → IR → PCRE, persistent memory, compositionality
   │
   ▼
Phase 2  20 QUESTIONS    active learning, EXCEPTION, information gain, persistent growth
   │
   ▼
Phase 3  GENERALIZATION  LLM kernel, distributed CODEX, φ numerics, multi-modal hooks
```

## The compounding contract (claim → artifact → test)

| Phase | Architectural claim tested | Reusable artifact left behind | Consumed from prior phases |
|-------|----------------------------|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
| 0 | The substrate is sound, versioned, inspectable. | `kainos.codex`, `kainos.ir`, `kainos.harness`, schema validation, golden tests | — |
| 1 | IR + CODEX yield *compositional* regex generation + *persistent* memory + *honest* uncertainty. | `kainos.lang` (deterministic kernel), `kainos.regex` (dialect + emitter + testgen), benchmark suite | CODEX, IR, harness |
| 2 | The system *actively acquires* knowledge and *shrinks EXCEPTION*; info-gain question selection; growth is persistent across restart. | `kainos.q20` (game loop, oracle, info-gain, learning loop), concept corpus | CODEX, IR, reasoner, harness |
| 3 | The same algebra generalizes: LLM kernel A/B, cross-node reconciliation, φ numerics (gated), multi-modal hooks, capability projection (X1/X2), recursive workspace (X3) | `kainos.exchange`, `kainos.numerics`, `kainos.multimodal` (stubs), `kainos.projection`, `kainos.workspace` | everything |

## Definition of "compounding" (measurable)

At each phase boundary, record:

- **Lines reused** from prior phase vs. lines newly written (target: reuse dominates).
- **Experiments re-run** against the same harness (no new harness per phase).
- **CODEX continuity**: the Phase 2 codex is the Phase 1 codex *continued*, not a new
  DB — same schema, same assertions, more knowledge.

## The claim registry (stable IDs, referenced everywhere)

Architectural claims get stable IDs so experiments, kill criteria (04-reality-check),
and results can cite them without ambiguity. **Never renumber or rename an ID.**

| ID | Claim | Proven in |
|----|-------|-----------|
| **C1** | Compositional generalization — novel *combinations* of learned abstractions are solved (train parts separately, test the combination) | Phase 1 (E1.2, E1.5) |
| **C2** | Persistent learning without retraining — teach → restart (frozen kernel) → still know | Phase 1 (E1.3), Phase 2 (E2.3) |
| **C3** | Honest uncertainty — the system escalates/asks at its knowledge boundary instead of emitting an unjustified answer | Phase 1 (E1.4) |
| **A1** | Active information-gain question selection beats random questioning (more wins, fewer questions) | Phase 2 (E2.1) |
| **A2** | EXCEPTION shrinkage — coverage rises and exception counts fall as the ontology grows | Phase 2 (E2.2) |
| **A3** | Cross-game learning — knowledge from earlier games improves later ones (persistence is worth more than a stateless re-derivation) | Phase 2 (E2.3) |
| **A4** | Compositional concept recognition — unseen concepts are identified from property conjunctions | Phase 2 (E2.4) |
| **A5** | Contradiction → missing dimension — a recurring conflict forces a *new context TERM* (ontology expansion), never averaged probabilities | Phase 2 (E2.5), Phase 3 (E3.3) |
| **X1** | Capability-faithful projection — the system plans only over *declared* capabilities; unachievable goals return NO VALID PLAN (named gap + nearest viable plan), never a hallucinated action | Phase 3 (E3.6) |
| **X2** | Structured creativity — temperature over *constrained* traversal yields varied but valid outputs; novelty never violates established facts | Phase 3 (E3.6) |
| **X3** | Recursive workspace memory — workspaces nest and are queryable ("what did we decide?"); nothing reaches the CODEX without an explicit, provenance-carrying promotion | Phase 3 (E3.7) |

North-star mapping (00-north-star): persistent memory=C2, compositionality=C1, honest
uncertainty=C3, inspectability=every experiment's evidence chain, compounding=reuse
stats per phase. **X1–X3** are the Phase-3 additions from the supplemental-ideas
integration (projection + recursive workspace); they extend — never supersede — the
C/A series. *Never renumber or rename an existing ID.*

## Exit criteria (every phase must satisfy all)

1. Named experiments run green in CI (see `40-testing/harness.md`).
2. Metrics reported as a table in the phase's `results.md`.
3. The phase's claim is demonstrated by evidence, not argument (P8).
4. Reusable artifacts merged into `src/kainos` with tests.
5. ADRs updated; no principle violated without an ADR (P1–P10).

## Ordering rationale

- Regex **first**: it has a *formal target language* — the
  computer itself judges correctness via execution + generated test cases. That
  gives a strong, objective training signal and a clean A/B baseline.
- 20Q **second**: it needs the persistent CODEX + reasoner from Phase 1, and it adds
  the *active* dimension (what to ask next) that regex doesn't exercise.
- Generalization **last**: only after the single-node loop is proven.

## P1.01 — Regex IR dialect models

- `src/kainos/regex/ir.py`: enums + dataclasses for the dialect

  `Alternative`, `Group`, `Flag`, `UnresolvedRef`) with `to_generic()/from_generic()`
  mapping to the Phase 0 generic IR.

  and back without loss.

## P1.02 — PCRE emitter

- `src/kainos/regex/emitter.py`: `emit(node) -> str` implementing spec.md §3 exactly.
- Escaping helper for `LITERAL`.
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_emitter.py` — table-driven tests for every rule +
  the two canonical examples from spec.md §3 (byte-exact).

## P1.03 — Deterministic language kernel

- `src/kainos/lang/deterministic.py`: `DeterministicKernel` implementing the
  `LanguageKernel` protocol (`parse`, `realize`, `propose`). Uses a small tokenizer +
  recursive-descent parser for spec.md §1. Emits `UNRESOLVED_REF` for vague terms.
- `src/kainos/lang/kernel.py`: the `LanguageKernel` protocol + `Interpretation`.
- **Verify:** `tests/lang/test_deterministic.py` — every clause template + every
  quantifier/class surface maps to the expected AST node.

  `source=seed_corpus, status=established`.

  the correct realization is returned; `dump` shows provenance on every assertion.

## P1.05 — Reasoner resolution step

- `src/kainos/regex/resolver.py`: walk the IR; for each node, query CODEX for its
  realization; for `UNRESOLVED_REF`, attempt **rotation** (spec.md §1.5) or mark
  `REQUIRES_CONTEXT` (→ escalation).
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_resolver.py` — "hyphen" resolves to `-`;
  "the dash thing" produces candidates and, when ambiguous, an escalation result.

## P1.06 — Test-case generator + judge

- `src/kainos/regex/testgen.py`: seeded positive/negative generator (spec.md §4).
- `src/kainos/regex/judge.py`: `compile` + `fullmatch` verdict with a diff of
  misjudged examples.
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_testgen.py` — generator covers every operator;
  judge rejects a deliberately wrong regex with a useful diff.

## P1.07 — End-to-end pipeline

- `src/kainos/regex/pipeline.py`: `describe(text) -> Result` composing
  kernel → IR → resolver → emitter → judge → trace.
- Result includes the **audit trace** (IR, resolved CODEX assertions, emitted PCRE,
  judge verdict) for C4.
- CLI: `kainos regex describe "..."` and `kainos regex explain "..."`.
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_pipeline.py` — the canonical example returns a
  passing verdict + trace.

## P1.08 — Seed corpus dataset

- `data/regex/seed_corpus.jsonl` (spec.md §3 canonical + every operator variant).
- A loader `src/kainos/regex/data.py`.
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_data.py` — corpus loads, is valid, unique ids, has
  `positive`/`negative` lists.

## P1.09 — E1.1 parity run

- Run pipeline over `seed_corpus`; write `results/phase-1/e1.1.json`.
- **Verify:** accuracy == 1.0; report table in `results.md`.

## P1.10 — Compositional set generator

- `src/kainos/regex/compose.py`: seeded cross-product of operators → novel
  descriptions + expected PCRE + tests (spec.md §4).
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_compose.py` — each generated item's expected PCRE
  passes the judge; assert no item duplicates a seed example.

## P1.11 — E1.2 compositionality vs. direct baseline

- Direct baseline = kernel → emitter with **no CODEX/resolver** (meanings hard-coded
  in the kernel), to isolate the CODEX's contribution.
- Run both over `compositional_set`; write `results/phase-1/e1.2.json`.
- **Verify:** threshold met (pipeline ≥ baseline + margin, pipeline ≥ 0.8).

- Teach `US_PHONE_NUMBER` assertion; `describe("an American phone number")` succeeds.

  CODEX); `describe` again succeeds.
- **Verify:** `tests/regex/test_persistence.py` — before/after both pass; explain

- `src/kainos/q20/game.py`: `Game` state machine (ask → answer → update → guess/end),

# action-steps/ — Executable task directives

This folder turns the plan in `plan/` into **self-contained, sequential, prompt-like
directives**. Each file is a single unit of work that can be handed to a fresh agent
(or pasted into an AI) and executed to completion.

## The zero-knowledge contract

Each directive is designed so you do **not** need to read `PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md` or the
full plan. You need at most two files:

1. **`00-CONTEXT.md`** — read once. The irreducible background (what we're building,
   the invariants, the repo layout, the conventions). ~1 page.
2. **The current directive** (e.g. `06-regex-ir-emitter.md`) — follow it top to bottom.

Pointers to `plan/…` files inside a directive are *optional* "if stuck" references,
never required reading.

**`LAYOUT.md`** is the optional cross-reference: which directive creates which durable
path, plus the directory conventions and any layout gaps to resolve before executing.

## How to use

- Work through the files **in numeric order**. Each lists its prerequisites.
  **Ordering exception (Phase 3):** `21-projection-planning.md` and
  `22-workspace-memory.md` run **before** `20-multimodal-final.md` — directive 20 is
  the final consolidation and always runs last, despite its number.
- A directive is **done** only when its "Done when" checklist is fully checked and its
  verification command passes.
- After finishing a directive, mark it done in the ledger below (change ⬜ → ✅).

# 00 — CONTEXT (read once)

This is the irreducible background for every directive in this folder. Read it once,
then follow any `NN-*.md` directive self-contained.

## What we're building

**Kainos-Logos** (καινός = new · λόγος = reason/order): a cognitive architecture where
a neural "language kernel" maps natural language ↔ a formal **Semantic IR**, and all
durable knowledge lives in a **CODEX** — an explicit, inspectable graph of TERMs +
typed relationships + provenance + context + time + epistemic state + an **EXCEPTION**
boundary. The neural model learns *how to operate on knowledge*; the CODEX
*accumulates the knowledge* — so the system keeps learning **without retraining**.

```text
text → LANGUAGE KERNEL → SEMANTIC IR → CODEX ⇄ REASONER → verified IR → REALIZER → text

Phase 3 adds two structures around this line (ADR-0011/0012):
  • WORKSPACE — recursive, lifetime-scoped containers of IRs (memory as queryable
    structure; explicit promotion into the CODEX — `plan/10-architecture/workspace-memory.md`)
  • PROJECTION — goal-directed planning over declared CAPABILITIES
    (Response = Realize(Project(Parse(Input), …)); NO VALID PLAN is a first-class
    result — `plan/10-architecture/projection.md`)
```

## The invariants (non-negotiable; code must respect these)

1. **Assertions, not facts** — the CODEX stores `subject--relation-->object` *wrapped
   in* source/provenance/context/validity/status. Never a bare edge.
2. **Neural model = language organ, not brain** — it does `text ↔ IR` and proposes
   hypotheses. It never stores durable knowledge.
3. **CODEX = single source of truth** for durable knowledge.
4. **Everything is a TERM** (independently addressable semantic node).
5. **EXCEPTION ≠ impossible** — unexplored valid combos vs. hard-constraint violations
   are categorically different.
6. **Contradiction is a signal** — preserve conflicts; drive ontology expansion, never
   average probabilities.
7. **Semantic IR decouples** the pipeline (any layer swappable).
8. **Measure, don't argue** — every claim is a benchmarked experiment.
9. **Inspectability is first-class** — every answer exposes its trace.
10. **Start small, scale later** — no premature generalization.
11. **Capabilities are declared, not implied** — the planner only uses declared
    capabilities; an unachievable goal returns NO VALID PLAN (gap + nearest viable
    plan), never a hallucinated action.
12. **Memory is recursively addressable structure; promotion is explicit** — working
    memory is nestable WORKSPACE containers of queryable IRs; nothing reaches the
    CODEX without a deliberate, provenance-carrying promotion.

## Critical vocabulary

- **TERM** — semantic node (concept/relation/operator/constraint/source/entity).
- **ASSERTION** — a relationship + mandatory metadata (source, context, validity
  interval, confidence, `status`, provenance). The atomic CODEX unit.
- **CODEX** — the persistent semantic store (SQLite-backed behind an interface).
- **Semantic IR** — JSON-serializable, versioned intermediate representation.
- **EXCEPTION** — a representable-but-unverified valid combination; states:
  `UNSEEN, UNRESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS, CONFLICTING, UNVERIFIED, REQUIRES_CONTEXT, IMPOSSIBLE`.
- **Epistemic states** (an assertion's `status`): `candidate, established, disputed,
  obsolete, hypothesis, ambiguous, contradicted, inapplicable`.

- **Toolchain:** run everything inside the pinned Docker image (ADR-0010); don't

# Action Step 02 — CODEX data model + store (P0.02–P0.03)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The CODEX persistence layer: assertion dataclasses (with mandatory provenance) and a
store interface with a SQLite implementation + an in-memory implementation.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Step 01 done (`import kainos` works).

## Background

The CODEX stores **assertions, not facts** (invariant #1). Every assertion carries
`source`, `context`, `status`, provenance, and (optionally) a validity interval and
EXCEPTION state. There is **no bare-edge path**. This is the substrate every later
phase depends on — get the model exactly right now.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/codex/models.py`

Frozen dataclasses:

- `TermRef(id: str, kind: str = "concept", labels: list[str] = field(default_factory=list))`
- `Context(data: dict)` — free-form but JSON-serializable
- `Interval(from: str | None, to: str | None)` — validity range
- `Source(uri: str, media_type: str | None = None, version: str | None = None,
  hash: str | None = None, retrieved_at: str | None = None, authority: str | None = None)`
- `EpistemicState(str, Enum)`: `candidate, established, disputed, obsolete,
  hypothesis, ambiguous, contradicted, inapplicable`
- `ExceptionState(str, Enum)`: `unseen, unresolved, ambiguous, conflicting,
  unverified, requires_context, impossible`
- `Provenance(source: Source, observer: str, derived: bool = False,
  verified: bool = False, evidence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list))`
- `Assertion(id: str, subject: TermRef, relation: TermRef, object: TermRef | str,
  polarity: bool = True, context: Context = field(default_factory=Context),
  validity: Interval | None = None, confidence: float = 1.0,
  status: EpistemicState = EpistemicState.candidate, provenance: Provenance,
  exception: ExceptionState | None = None)`

Rules to implement in `__post_init__`:
- **Non-nullable** (invariant #1): raise `TypeError` if `provenance` is missing and if
  `provenance.source` is missing. (`context` and `status` have defaults, so only
  `provenance`/`source` are strictly enforced.)
- `confidence` clamped to `[0.0, 1.0]`.
- `to_dict()` / `from_dict()` round-trip exactly (deterministic key order).

### 2. `specs/codex.schema.json` (G1)

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) named `kainos/codex/1` — the structural mirror of the
model above:

- `Assertion` required: `id`, `subject`, `relation`, `object`, `status`, `provenance`
  — `provenance` itself requires `source` (with `source.uri`) and `observer`
  (ADR-0008: no bare-edge escape hatch, enforced *by schema* too).
- Optional: `polarity`, `context`, `validity` (`from`/`to`), `confidence`,
  `exception` (enum: `unseen, unresolved, ambiguous, conflicting, unverified,
  requires_context, impossible`).
- The dataclasses remain the implementation source of truth; the schema is the
  *contract*. Add a parity test: every `to_dict()` output in the model test suite
  validates against `specs/codex.schema.json`.

### 3. `src/kainos/codex/store.py`

`CodexStore` protocol (methods, no logic):

```python
class CodexStore(Protocol):
    def add(self, a: Assertion) -> str: ...
    def update_status(self, id: str, status: EpistemicState,
                      evidence: list[str] | None = None) -> None: ...
    def query(self, *, subject: str | None = None, relation: str | None = None,
              object: str | None = None, status: EpistemicState | None = None,
              context_match: dict | None = None, time_at: str | None = None) -> list[Assertion]: ...
    def neighbors(self, term: str, depth: int = 1) -> list[Assertion]: ...
    def rotate(self, term: str) -> list[TermRef]: ...
    def coverage(self, term: str, context: Context | None = None) -> float: ...
    def dump(self) -> dict: ...
    def explain(self, id: str) -> dict: ...
```

### 4. `src/kainos/codex/sqlite.py` — `SqliteCodexStore`

SQLite schema:

```sql
CREATE TABLE terms (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT, labels TEXT /*JSON*/);
CREATE TABLE assertions (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, subject TEXT, relation TEXT, object TEXT,
  polarity INTEGER, context TEXT /*JSON*/, validity_from TEXT, validity_to TEXT,
  confidence REAL, status TEXT, provenance TEXT /*JSON*/, exception TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE evidence (assertion_id TEXT, evidence_id TEXT);
CREATE INDEX idx_subj ON assertions(subject, relation, object);
CREATE INDEX idx_rel  ON assertions(relation);
CREATE INDEX idx_stat ON assertions(status);
```

- `add` upserts the term rows and inserts the assertion (serialized via `to_dict`).
- `query` builds a parameterized `WHERE` from the provided filters; `context_match`
  is a substring/`LIKE` match over the context JSON; `time_at` checks
  `validity_from <= t <= validity_to` (inclusive, null = open-ended).
- `dump` returns `{"terms": [...], "assertions": [...]}` with deterministic ordering.

### 5. `src/kainos/codex/memory.py` — `InMemoryCodexStore`

Same protocol, backed by dicts/lists (for fast tests). Keep behavior identical to the
SQLite impl for `query`/`neighbors`/`coverage`.

### 6. Tests

`tests/codex/test_models.py`:
- construct a full assertion → `to_dict` → `from_dict` → equal.
- missing `provenance` raises `TypeError`; missing `source` raises `TypeError`.
- `confidence` clamps to `[0,1]`.
- every `to_dict()` output validates against `specs/codex.schema.json` (parity).

`tests/codex/test_store.py` (run against BOTH impls via `pytest.mark.parametrize`
over `[SqliteCodexStore, InMemoryCodexStore]`):
- add two assertions, `query(relation=...)` returns both.
- add a **disputed pair** (`CAPITAL_OF(France,Paris)` and
  `CAPITAL_OF(France,Lyon)`), query returns **both** (invariant #6: no averaging).

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/codex -q
```

Expect: all green, including the disputed-pair assertion surviving in both stores.

## Done when

- [ ] `models.py`, `store.py`, `sqlite.py`, `memory.py` exist
- [ ] `specs/codex.schema.json` exists; model ⇄ schema parity test green
- [ ] `pytest tests/codex -q` green
- [ ] disputed pair survives (both returned) in both impls
- [ ] non-nullable provenance enforced (missing source raises)

# Action Step 03 — CODEX explain + Semantic IR codec (P0.04–P0.05)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

(a) `explain(assertion_id)` returns an assertion with its evidence chain (inspectability);
(b) a versioned Semantic IR with JSON-Schema validation and a codec.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Step 02 done (`kainos.codex` works, disputed-pair test green).

## Background

Inspectability is a first-class feature (invariant #9): every conclusion must expose
its trace. The Semantic IR is the JSON-serializable, versioned structure all layers
speak (invariant #7) — it must be validated at every boundary so a malformed IR can't
silently corrupt downstream reasoning.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/codex/explain.py`

```python
def explain(store, id: str, depth: int = 3) -> dict:
    """Return assertion dict + provenance + evidence chain (recursive, depth-limited)."""
```

- Resolve the assertion; include its `provenance`; for each id in
  `provenance.evidence`, recurse (up to `depth`) and collect a `chain` list.
- Never raise on missing evidence — represent as `{"id": ..., "missing": True}`.
- Wire `explain` into both store impls (`SqliteCodexStore.explain`,
  `InMemoryCodexStore.explain`) so the protocol's `explain` is satisfied.

### 2. `specs/ir.schema.json`

JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) named `kainos/ir/1` with:

- top-level `object`; required `["kind"]`; `kind` enum
  `["state","pattern","query","command"]`;
- optional arrays: `goals`, `entities`, `relationships`, `events`, `constraints`,
  `unresolved`, `hypotheses`; optional `meta` object;
- `entities[].id` required (string), `type` (string), `labels` (array of string);
- `relationships[]` required `subject`, `relation`, `object` (strings), optional
  `context` (object);
- `constraints[]` required `kind` (string), optional `value`;
- `unresolved[]` required `id`, `surface`, optional `candidates` (array of string).

### 3. `src/kainos/ir/models.py`

`SemanticIR` (a thin wrapper over the validated dict) + small dataclasses
`Entity`, `Relationship`, `Constraint`, `UnresolvedRef`, `Hypothesis`, `Goal` — each
with `to_dict/from_dict`. Keep them minimal; the schema is the source of truth.

### 4. `src/kainos/ir/codec.py`

```python
def validate(data: dict) -> None          # raises ValueError with schema path on failure
def load(data: dict) -> SemanticIR        # validate + wrap
def dump(ir: SemanticIR) -> dict          # unwrap (deterministic)
```

- Use `jsonschema` (add `jsonschema` to dev deps if not present).
- Bundle `specs/ir.schema.json` with the package (via `importlib.resources`) so
  `validate` doesn't depend on CWD.

### 5. Tests

- `tests/codex/test_explain.py`: seed two assertions where B is evidence for A; assert
  `explain(A)` includes B in its chain; assert a missing evidence id doesn't raise.
- `tests/ir/test_codec.py`: a valid sample loads; a dict missing `kind` raises with a
  schema path in the message; `dump(load(x)) == x` for a fixture.
- Add `tests/ir/golden/minimal.json` — a minimal valid state IR committed as a fixture.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/codex/test_explain.py tests/ir/test_codec.py -q
```

Expect: all green.

## Done when

- [ ] `explain` returns evidence chain (and is wired into both stores)
- [ ] `specs/ir.schema.json` exists; `validate` rejects malformed IR with a path
- [ ] `dump(load(x)) == x` for the fixture
- [ ] `pytest tests/codex/test_explain.py tests/ir/test_codec.py -q` green

`plan/10-architecture/semantic-ir.md`, `plan/30-phases/phase-0-foundation/actions.md` → P0.04–P0.05.

# Action Step 06 — Regex IR dialect + PCRE emitter (P1.01–P1.02)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The regex-dialect AST nodes (as a specialization of the generic Semantic IR) and a
PCRE emitter that translates them deterministically.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 01–05 done (Phase 0 complete).

## Background

This is the first "real" phase. The AST is the Semantic IR's regex **dialect**; the
emitter is a *dumb* rule-applier — meaning lives in the CODEX (step 07), not here.
The emitter must be byte-exact for the canonical examples (they become tests).

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/regex/ir.py`

Enums + nodes for the dialect:

```
Node (base)
Sequence(elements: list[Node])
Repeat(node: Node, quantifier: Quantifier)
Class(kind: ClassKind)                 # digit, letter, word, whitespace, any
Literal(text: str)
Anchor(kind: AnchorKind)               # start, end
Alternative(branches: list[Node])
Group(node: Node)
Flag(name: str)                        # e.g. "case_insensitive"
UnresolvedRef(surface: str, candidates: list[str])
Quantifier (enum): one_or_more, zero_or_more, optional, exactly(n), at_least(n), at_most(n), between(a,b)
```

Each node implements `to_generic() -> dict` and `from_generic(dict) -> Node`, mapping
onto the generic IR: a node is an `entity` with a `type` from this dialect's enum,
wired by `relationships` (`sequence`, `repeat`, `alternative_branch`, `flag`). The
generic→dialect round-trip must be lossless (test it).

### 2. `src/kainos/regex/emitter.py`

`emit(node: Node) -> str` per this table (byte-exact):

| AST | PCRE |
|-----|------|
| `Sequence(a,b,c)` | elements **concatenated, unwrapped**: `a b c` |
| `Repeat(n, one_or_more)` | `n+` |
| `Repeat(n, zero_or_more)` | `n*` |
| `Repeat(n, optional)` | `n?` |
| `Repeat(n, exactly(k))` | `n{k}` |
| `Repeat(n, at_least(k))` | `n{k,}` |
| `Repeat(n, at_most(k))` | `n{0,k}` |
| `Repeat(n, between(a,b))` | `n{a,b}` |
| `Class(digit)` | `\d` |
| `Class(letter)` | `[A-Za-z]` |
| `Class(word)` | `\w` |
| `Class(whitespace)` | `\s` |
| `Class(any)` | `.` |
| `Literal(s)` | `s` with regex metachars `\.^$*+?()[]{}|` escaped |
| `Anchor(start)` | `^` |
| `Anchor(end)` | `$` |
| `Alternative(a,b)` | `(?:a|b)` |
| `Group(n)` | `(?:n)` |
| `Flag(case_insensitive)` | prefix `(?i)` |

`UnresolvedRef` has no PCRE — emitting one must **raise** `UnresolvedError` (never
guess; the resolver in step 08 resolves it first).

### 3. Tests

`tests/regex/test_ir.py`: every node round-trips generic→dialect losslessly.
`tests/regex/test_emitter.py`: table-driven — every rule above; plus the two canonical
examples (byte-exact):
- `Sequence[Literal("cat"), Repeat(Class(digit), one_or_more)]` → `cat\d+`
- `Flag(case_insensitive) + Sequence[Repeat(Class(digit), exactly 3), Literal("-"),
  Alternative(Literal("foo"), Literal("bar"))]` → `(?i)\d{3}-(?:foo|bar)`
- emitting an `UnresolvedRef` raises.

Note: sequences emit as plain concatenation — only `Group`/`Alternative` add `(?:…)`
wrapping. (An earlier draft row `Sequence(a,b,c) → (?:a)(?:b)(?:c)` contradicted both
canonical examples and is corrected here; the authoritative table is in
`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §3.)

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/regex -q
```

Expect: all green, canonical examples byte-exact.

## Done when

- [ ] `ir.py` + `emitter.py` exist; generic↔dialect round-trip lossless
- [ ] all emitter rules green, including canonical examples (byte-exact)
- [ ] `UnresolvedRef` emit raises
- [ ] `pytest tests/regex -q` green

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §2–§3 (the authoritative tables).

# Action Step 07 — Deterministic language kernel + CODEX lexicon (P1.03–P1.04)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

A deterministic parser that turns restricted-English regex descriptions into the
dialect AST, plus the lexicon seeded into the CODEX (so *meaning* lives in the CODEX,
not in the parser).

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Step 06 done (dialect + emitter).

## Background

The kernel is the "language organ" (invariant #2): `text ↔ IR` only. For Phase 1 it is
**deterministic** (hand-written grammar) so the compositionality experiment isn't
confounded by an LLM's latent regex knowledge. The lexicon (what "hyphen"/"digit"
*mean*) goes in the CODEX, not in the parser — that's the whole point.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/lang/kernel.py`

```python
@dataclass
class Interpretation:
    ir: object            # a regex dialect Node (later: generic SemanticIR)
    score: float
    unresolved: list[str]

class LanguageKernel(Protocol):
    def parse(self, text: str, context: dict | None = None) -> list[Interpretation]: ...
    def realize(self, ir, style: str | None = None) -> str: ...
    def propose(self, ir) -> list[dict]: ...
```

### 2. `src/kainos/lang/deterministic.py` — `DeterministicKernel`

Implement a small tokenizer + recursive-descent parser for this grammar (from
`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §1):

- **Clause templates:** `<anchor>`, `<quant> <class>`, `the literal <text>`,
  `a hyphen` / any bare content word (lexicon-ref, see below), `either <a> or <b>`,
  `a group of (…)`, `ignoring case`, `<connector> <clause>`.
- **Quantifier surface → value:** `one or more`→one_or_more; `zero or more`→zero_or_more;
  `optional|maybe|optionally`→optional; `exactly N | N`→exactly(N); `at least N`→at_least(N);
  `at most N`→at_most(N); `between N and M | from N to M`→between(N,M).
- **Class surface → node:** digit(s)/number(s)→digit; letter(s)→letter; word→word;
  whitespace/space(s)→whitespace; any/anything→any.
  **Disambiguation:** bare "number(s)" → `Literal` when a standalone numeral follows;
  else `Class(digit)`; if truly ambiguous → `UnresolvedRef` with both candidates.
- **Connectors:** `followed by|then|and|,` → sequence continuation; `or|either…or` →
  alternative.
- **Reference terms:** `thing`, `the … thing`, `it`, `that` → `UnresolvedRef(surface,
  candidates=["digit_class","numeric_literal",…])`.
- Anchors: `beginning/start of string` → Anchor(start); `end of string` → Anchor(end).
- `realize(ir)` = emit(ir) (reuse step 06 emitter).
- `propose(ir)` = `[]` for now (the reasoner proposes in step 08).
- **Lexicon-reference semantics (important):** the parser assigns **no character
  values**, ever. Class surfaces keep semantic class identity; a content word
  (`hyphen`, `dash`, …) is resolved at parse time by a **direct CODEX lexicon
  lookup** (exact `realizes_as` → `Literal(realization)`). A miss or an ambiguous
  hit yields `UnresolvedRef`, which the step-08 resolver handles by rotation or
  escalation. (Authoritative wording: `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §1.)

Keep it a pure function of text → AST; **do not** hard-code "hyphen means `-`" here.

### 3. Seed the lexicon into the CODEX

`src/kainos/regex/lexicon.py` — `seed(codex)`: add assertions (provenance
`Source(uri="seed_corpus", version="1")`, `status=established`) for:

```
"hyphen"       --realizes_as--> "-"
"digit"        --realizes_as--> "\d"
"letter"       --realizes_as--> "[A-Za-z]"
"word"         --realizes_as--> "\w"
"whitespace"   --realizes_as--> "\s"
"any"          --realizes_as--> "."
"start"        --realizes_as--> "^"
"end"          --realizes_as--> "$"
```

### 4. Tests

- `tests/lang/test_deterministic.py`: every clause template + every quantifier/class
  surface → expected AST node. Include "three digits, then a hyphen" → Sequence of
  Repeat(digit, exactly 3) then Literal("-") (the hyphen came from the lexicon, not the parser).
- **Lexicon↔emitter parity test:** for every seeded `realizes_as` target, the
  emitter's output for the corresponding node equals the CODEX realization — the
  CODEX is the single source of truth for what a term means (invariant #2); the
  emitter's built-in class table is held consistent by this test (spec §5).
- `tests/regex/test_codex_seed.py`: after `seed()`, query each class/literal and assert
  the realization; `dump()` shows `status=established` + `source=seed_corpus` on every
  seeded assertion (invariant #1).

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/lang/test_deterministic.py tests/regex/test_codex_seed.py -q
```

Expect: all green.

## Done when

- [ ] `LanguageKernel` protocol + `DeterministicKernel` parse/realize/propose
- [ ] every grammar template + quantifier/class surface maps correctly
- [ ] lexicon lives in CODEX (with provenance), not in the parser
- [ ] `pytest tests/lang/test_deterministic.py tests/regex/test_codex_seed.py -q` green

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §1 (grammar) and §5 (CODEX role).

# Action Step 08 — Resolver + testgen/judge + pipeline (P1.05–P1.07)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The end-to-end pipeline: resolve the AST against the CODEX, emit PCRE, generate test
cases, execute, and return a verdict **with an audit trace**.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 06–07 done (emitter + kernel + lexicon).

## Background

The resolver is where the architecture earns its keep: an `UnresolvedRef` ("the dash
thing") is resolved by **rotation** through the CODEX or escalated. The judge is the
objective arbiter — it *executes* the regex against generated examples, so "correct"
means "matches the intended language", not "looks plausible".

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/regex/resolver.py`

`resolve(node: Node, codex) -> Resolved` where `Resolved = (node, trace: list[dict])`.

- Walk the AST. For each `Class`, look up its `realizes_as` in the CODEX (lexicon from
  step 07) and record a trace entry `{term, realized_as, assertion_id}`.
- For `UnresolvedRef`, attempt **rotation**: query CODEX neighbors of each candidate;
  if exactly one candidate's realization is reachable → resolve to it; if several →
  keep as unresolved and record `status=REQUIRES_CONTEXT` with candidates; if none →
  `UNSEEN`.
- Any remaining unresolved at the end → return an **escalation result** (see pipeline).

### 2. `src/kainos/regex/testgen.py` (seeded, deterministic)

`generate(node, seed=0) -> (positive: list[str], negative: list[str])`

- Positive: instantiate each node with concrete strings (digit→`0`, letter→`a`,
  literal→itself); expand quantifiers to a few lengths within bounds.
- Negative: mutate exactly one element (wrong class, out-of-range count, wrong
  literal, missing anchor, extra suffix) to violate one constraint.
- Deterministic under a fixed `seed`.

### 3. `src/kainos/regex/judge.py` + Perl judge (ADR-0009)

- `judge(pcre: str, positive, negative) -> Verdict` **invokes a Perl script**
  (`scripts/judge.pl`) that compiles the pattern and full-matches each example,
  returning JSON. The Perl engine is canonical (ADR-0009); Python `re` is not used.
- `Verdict(ok, mismatches=[...])` with a human-readable diff of any misjudged example.

### 4. `src/kainos/regex/pipeline.py`

`describe(text: str) -> Result` composing: `parse → resolve → emit → generate → judge`.
`Result` = `{ir, resolved_trace, pcre, verdict, escalation, confidence}`.

- If `resolve` found unresolved refs → set `escalation = {"status": "requires_context",
  "candidates": [...], "recommended_action": "ask_human"}` and do **not** emit a
  regex (invariant: never emit what you can't justify).
- Otherwise emit + judge, with `confidence` from the trace.

### 5. CLI

`kainos regex describe "..."` and `kainos regex explain "..."` (explain prints the full
IR + trace + PCRE + verdict).

### 6. Tests

- `tests/regex/test_resolver.py`: "hyphen" resolves to `-` via CODEX; "the dash thing"
  yields candidates and (when ambiguous) an escalation result.
- `tests/regex/test_testgen.py`: generator covers every operator; judge rejects a
  deliberately wrong regex with a useful diff.
- `tests/regex/test_pipeline.py`: canonical example returns `ok` + a non-empty trace;
  a vague description returns escalation (not a guessed regex).

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/regex -q && kainos regex describe "three digits, then a hyphen, then two letters"
```

Expect: all green; the CLI prints a passing verdict + trace.

## Done when

- [ ] resolver resolves via CODEX and escalates when ambiguous
- [ ] testgen + judge deterministic and useful
- [ ] pipeline returns verdict + full audit trace; escalates instead of guessing
- [ ] `kainos regex describe` / `explain` work
- [ ] `pytest tests/regex -q` green

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/spec.md` §4–§5, `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/actions.md` → P1.05–P1.07.

# Action Step 09 — Seed corpus + E1.1 parity (P1.08–P1.09)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

A hand-authored seed corpus covering every operator, and proof (E1.1) that the pipeline
achieves 100% parity on it.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 06–08 done (full pipeline works).

## Background

The seed corpus is the *explicit form* of the grammar — the only thing the
deterministic kernel is "trained" on. E1.1 is the first claim gate: the pipeline must
translate every seed description exactly. Do not proceed to compositionality until
parity is exact.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/regex/data.py`

`load_corpus(path) -> list[dict]` — each record
`{id, description, expected_pcre, positive: [str], negative: [str]}`.

### 2. `data/regex/seed_corpus.jsonl`

Author ~40–80 records, one per operator + representative combinations. Must cover:
every quantifier (one_or_more, zero_or_more, optional, exactly N, at_least N, at_most N,
between N M), every class, both anchors, `Literal` (incl. a metachar like `.` to test
escaping), `Alternative`, `Group`, `Flag(case_insensitive)`. Include the two canonical
examples from step 06. Each record needs non-empty `positive` and `negative` lists.

### 3. E1.1 runner

`src/kainos/regex/bench.py` — `run_e1_1()`: for each corpus record, `describe` it,
compare `pcre` to `expected_pcre` **and** judge against `positive`/`negative`.
Write `results/phase-1/e1.1.json` with `{config, accuracy, per_item:[{id, ok, pcre, expected}]}`.

Register E1.1 in the harness registry (`kainos.harness.runner.REGISTRY`) with
`name="e1.1"`, `metric="accuracy"`, `threshold="== 1.0"`.

## Verification

```bash
kainos experiment run --name e1.1 && python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('results/phase-1/e1.1.json'));print(d['accuracy'])"
```

Expect: `accuracy == 1.0`.

## Done when

- [ ] seed corpus covers every operator (assert in a test: all operators present)
- [ ] E1.1 accuracy == 1.0
- [ ] `results/phase-1/e1.1.json` written with config + per-item details
- [ ] harness registry includes `e1.1`

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/benchmarks.md`, `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/experiments.md` → E1.1.

# Action Step 10 — Compositional set + E1.2 (P1.10–P1.11)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

Prove compositional generalization (C1): the pipeline solves **novel combinations** of
known operators — combos that never appeared together in the seed corpus — and beats a
no-CODEX baseline.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 06–09 done (E1.1 parity == 1.0).

## Background

This is the core architectural claim. A conventional system that memorized the seed
data should *fail* on unseen operator combinations; the IR+CODEX pipeline should
*succeed*, because it composes known abstractions rather than recalling whole patterns.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/regex/compose.py`

`generate_compositional_set(seed_corpus, n=40, seed=42) -> list[dict]`
- Take a cross-product of operators (e.g. `three digits` + `optional` + `hyphen` +
  `two letters`) and build descriptions that **no single seed record** contains.
- Each output record: `{id, description, expected_pcre, positive, negative}` with
  `expected_pcre` verified by the judge (so the set is ground-truthed).
- **Assert no duplicate** of a seed description (compare normalized descriptions).
- **Materialize** the ground-truthed set to `data/regex/compositional_set.jsonl`
  (committed; deterministic under seed 42). It must be an on-disk artifact, not an
  in-memory-only object, so E1.2 and the E1.5 hold-out are auditable and reproducible
  (G2).

### 2. Baseline (no CODEX)

`src/kainos/regex/baseline.py` — `DirectBaseline`: kernel → emitter with **hard-coded**
class/literal meanings (no resolver/CODEX). It can't resolve `UnresolvedRef` and will
fail on anything the seed grammar didn't hard-code. This isolates the CODEX's
contribution (it's the "Model A" stand-in for the deterministic comparison; the full
LLM A/B is step 12).

### 3. E1.2 runner

`run_e1_2()`: run pipeline vs `DirectBaseline` on the compositional set; write
`results/phase-1/e1.2.json` with `{pipeline_accuracy, baseline_accuracy, margin}`.

## Verification

```bash
kainos experiment run --name e1.2 && python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('results/phase-1/e1.2.json'));print(d['pipeline_accuracy'], d['baseline_accuracy'])"
```

Expect: `pipeline_accuracy ≥ 0.8` **and** `pipeline_accuracy ≥ baseline_accuracy + 0.1`.

## Done when

- [ ] compositional set generated, ground-truthed, no seed duplicates (asserted)
- [ ] `data/regex/compositional_set.jsonl` committed (deterministic, seed 42)
- [ ] `DirectBaseline` (no CODEX) implemented
- [ ] E1.2 thresholds met (pipeline ≥ 0.8, pipeline ≥ baseline + margin)
- [ ] `results/phase-1/e1.2.json` written

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/experiments.md` → E1.2; `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/benchmarks.md` → A/B protocol.

# Action Step 11 — Persistent memory + honest uncertainty (P1.12–P1.13)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

Two demonstrations: (C2) a CODEX entry survives a full restart and is reused with
frozen neural weights; (C3) underspecified input is recognized and escalated, never
hallucinated.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 06–10 done.

## Background

C2 is the emotional center of the whole project: knowledge separated from weights.
C3 is the "when should the AI stop pretending it knows?" behavior. Both are what make
this *not* just another regex generator.

## Steps

### 1. Persistent-memory teaching (C2)

- Teach the CODEX: `US_PHONE_NUMBER --realizes_as--> "\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}"`
  (provenance `Source(uri="user_instruction", version="1")`, `status=established`).
- `describe("an American phone number")` → succeeds (kernel has no rule for
  "phone number"; the resolver finds it via CODEX).
- **Restart:** dump CODEX to disk → construct a *fresh* pipeline (same kernel code,
  reloaded CODEX) → `describe` again → succeeds.
- Test `tests/regex/test_persistence.py` asserts both runs pass and `explain` shows
  the provenance.

### 2. Vague-set + escalation (C3)

- `data/regex/vague_set.jsonl`: ~10 deliberately underspecified descriptions
  ("…then the dash thing…", "start with the number thing, three of them…").
- Run pipeline; for each, expect either (a) resolved via rotation, or (b) escalation
  (`recommended_action == "ask_human"`), and **never** an unjustified regex.
- Metrics: `clarification_rate = escalated/total`, `justified_rate = (emitted with
  complete trace)/emitted`.

### 3. E1.3 / E1.4 runners

- `run_e1_3()` → `results/phase-1/e1.3.json` (`before`, `after`, `assertion_present`).
- `run_e1_4()` → `results/phase-1/e1.4.json` (`clarification_rate`, `justified_rate`).
- Register `e1.3`, `e1.4` in the harness registry.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/regex/test_persistence.py -q && kainos experiment run --name e1.4 && python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('results/phase-1/e1.4.json'));print(d['clarification_rate'], d['justified_rate'])"
```

Expect: persistence test green; `clarification_rate ≥ 0.5` and `justified_rate == 1.0`.

## Done when

- [ ] C2: teach → succeed → restart → succeed, with provenance shown
- [ ] C3: vague set escalates (or resolves via rotation); never unjustified
- [ ] E1.3 + E1.4 thresholds met; results written

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/experiments.md` → E1.3, E1.4.

# Action Step 12 — LLM baseline + E1.5 A/B + Phase 1 sign-off (P1.14–P1.16)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The headline A/B: a conventional next-token model (Model A) vs. the CODEX pipeline
(Model B) on combinations absent from training — plus the Phase 1 sign-off.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Steps 06–11 done (E1.1–E1.4 green).

## Background

E1.5 is the falsification experiment: same data, same budget, only the architecture
differs. Model B (this project) should win on *unseen combinations*, because it
composes abstractions instead of recalling patterns.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/lang/llm.py` — `LLMKernel`

Behind the **same** `LanguageKernel` protocol. **Runtime (locked —
`plan/04-reality-check.md` §5): local `llama-server` + one pinned small GGUF, fully
offline** on the Strix Halo host (CPU/Vulkan; no hosted APIs in the experiment pin).
`parse(text)` prompts the model to output the dialect AST as JSON → validate against
`specs/ir.schema.json` → `from_generic`. Keep it a thin adapter; do not change the
protocol.

### 2. Model A baseline

`scripts/train_baseline.py`: train a tiny seq2seq/transformer on `English → PCRE` pairs
from the **seed corpus only** (the compositional set is held out). `scripts/predict.py`
runs inference. Model A must **not** see the CODEX path.

### 3. E1.5 runner

`run_e1_5()`: run Model A and Model B on **`data/regex/holdout_set.jsonl`** +
`vague_set`. **Materialize** `holdout_set.jsonl` from the committed
`data/regex/compositional_set.jsonl` (deterministic split — record the rule/seed in
the result `config`; never re-derive it ad hoc). Write `results/phase-1/e1.5.json`
(accuracies, per-item diff) and `results/phase-1/e1.5.md` (report). Compare with a
statistical note (e.g. exact McNemar's test on matched items if sample size permits;
otherwise report the raw gap + per-item table).

### 4. Phase 1 sign-off

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/results.md`: E1.1–E1.5 tables, exit-criteria mapping,
and **reuse stats** (P0 artifacts consumed: codex/ir/harness LOC reused vs. new).

## Verification

```bash
kainos experiment run --name e1.5 && cat results/phase-1/e1.5.md
```

Expect: `pipeline_accuracy > baseline_accuracy` (significant), and B also abstains
correctly on the vague set (which A cannot).

## Done when

- [ ] `LLMKernel` behind the protocol (mocked-backend test green); runtime = pinned
      local GGUF, offline (reality-check §5)
- [ ] Model A baseline trains on seed data only (compositional held out)
- [ ] `data/regex/holdout_set.jsonl` materialized + committed (E1.5 gate input)
- [ ] E1.5 thresholds met (B > A; B abstains correctly on vague set)
- [ ] `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/results.md` signs off all exit criteria

## Phase 1 is DONE after this step.

Mark steps 06–12 ✅; proceed to `13-q20-corpus-oracle.md`.

`plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/experiments.md` → E1.5; `plan/30-phases/phase-1-regex/benchmarks.md` → A/B protocol.
